title: Derived vanishing from homotopy vanishing
statement: Let A be an abelian category and P,K complexes in A. Suppose P is bounded (its terms vanish outside some integer interval) and every term of P is projective. If every morphism from P to K in the homotopy category maps to zero under the derived localization Qh, every morphism from Q(P) to Q(K) in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is zero.

proof.text: Use the bounded-above projective hypothesis to obtain a K-projective structure. The comparison bijection Qh_map_bijective represents each derived morphism by a homotopy-category morphism; transport along quotientCompQhIso and cancel the two isomorphisms.

theorem precise_vanishing_of_homotopy_zero
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (P K : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (hPbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (P.X i)))
    (hPprojective : ∀ i : ℤ, Projective (P.X i))
    (hzero : ∀ g :
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K),
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map g = 0) :
    ∀ f : (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K), f = 0
